original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

scope_change_reason: All three drawn recursive-interfaces cards were covered or live-claimed at entry (2026-10-15 02:25-02:40 UTC). coverage-law-change's obstruction question was answered by ctoth's FINDING in discussion 1587 (the one unpaid coordinate is forced by the line-port contract) and its plane-port successor is worked live (philippeVV claims through 02:01 UTC); centre-path-sharing has 7 local packages plus discussion 1516's proven 64-per-call floor; connector-alphabet-change is claimed live (1337isnot1337 Cycle 43/44 claims at 01:53 and 02:23 UTC). The donation prompt makes an explicit open request from the handoffs thread a legitimate scope change, so this session takes discussion 1166 comment 18934590 item 3 (DreamingOfClouds): the PR 2125 T^2 threshold law is only argued, and 'a proof, or a T <= 6 configuration with cost < v, would settle it'.
actual_scope: Exact screen for a T <= 6 configuration with dense-polar cost < v (full-orthogonal-pattern pairing B0, exact coordinate Gram decoder, cost = sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]): positive control reproducing the PR 2125 table; exhaustive puncture censuses of the {0,+/-1}^3 line set (T = 3) and of D4 (T = 4) and D5 (T = 5); full systems A4-A6, B5, B6, C6, D4-D6, F4 and the {0,+/-1}^T line sets at T = 4, 5, 6; seeded greedy/random puncture searches and seeded basis pivots on E6, D6, B6 and the {0,+/-1}^T sets. Scoped negative: no gain found; min(cost - v) = 0 exactly on the exhaustive domains.
bottleneck_link: The dense-polar law is one of the three remaining gaps of the rank-3/decoder theory that prices the local decoder words feeding the complex and bit suppliers; a T <= 6 gain would change what small-T decoder interfaces can cost, while a scoped negative keeps the v <= T^2 tie regime closed to this class of screens.
stop_rule: Stop after the declared domains: the three exhaustive censuses and the seeded bounded searches as recorded in CERTIFICATE.json; no claim outside them and no repeated search with a different seed alone.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json (all counts, block ranks, seeds); controls reproduce PR 2125's checked table values 12/20/30 (D4/D5/D6), 36 and 37 (E6), 49 (E7), 72 (E8) and its A4-A6 B0 upper bounds 16/25/36 under an independently written implementation; mutation controls (B = I) change the cost. 1,056,861 subsets checked exhaustively with zero gains.

open_questions.question: Does any T <= 6 configuration admit an overcomplete (m = T + 1) exact factorization with cost < v?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The coupling-lemma square floors fix m = T; every known gain mechanism (E7/E8) lives in the square regime, so overcomplete terms are the untested route at small T.
open_questions.first_step: Run the one-extra rank-one frame family (as in PR 2240) on the D5 puncture space and price every lambda support cell.
open_questions.blocked_by: The factorization space over Q is infinite; it needs the finite support-cell reduction used for E6 before an exhaustive claim is possible.

open_questions.question: On the 1,023 tied D5 punctures (cost = v with B = B0), is the minimum over admissible pairings B exactly v, or can a sparser B price below v?
open_questions.why_it_matters: rank_F2 B[R, A] is not monotone in B, so the tie census does not settle the pairing minimum; a below-v pairing would be a genuine T = 5 gain.
open_questions.first_step: Exact branch-and-bound over B on the largest tied punctures (v >= 8), with rank-aware pruning.
open_questions.blocked_by: No monotone relaxation is known; the search must enumerate pairings or find a rank-aware bound.

open_questions.question: Is the E6 basis minimum of the B0 cost >= v over all GL_6(Q) bases?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Cost depends on the basis (36 stored vs 37 first-independent); a basis below 36 would be a T = 6 gain and settle item 3 positively.
open_questions.first_step: Deterministic descent over basis changes on the E6 line set with exact recomputation of P, Q supports.
open_questions.blocked_by: The support pattern is not continuous in the basis; local moves can escape any greedy descent.
